newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - March 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - March 20.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on March 20. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Parliamentary speaker Wahono said there was no prohibition against discussing possible candidates for the vice-president's post and the current discussion about candidates showed an increased democratic awareness in the community.
President Suharto told Australia's new ambassador to Jakarta John McCarthy that he hoped the different political systems in the two countries would not become an obstacle for future cooperation.
More than 50,000 people from across East Timor flocked to the town of Baucau to watch the colourful inauguration of Bishop Basilio do Nascimento.

The World Customs Organisation has warned that overworked and underpaid customs officials could bring about negative impacts on a country's international trade because such conditions promoted bribery and corruption.
Ismail Hasan Metareum, head of the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP), said he would consider standing for the vice-president's position if his party proposed him.
A meeting of Indonesian social scientists has been told their advice is often ignored if it is critical of the government.
